svg.text: Phoenix SoC: Top-Level Architecture Block Diagram
A modular 32-bit RISC-V system-on-chip with a self-recovery-oriented architecture
Harit Patel, Mokshit Lattha | Mentor: Dr. Gunjan Thakur
19 November 2026 | Status: architecture frozen, verified in a pre-RTL model; RTL not yet written
triple modular redundancy, cores in lockstep
bus outputs of A, B, C (103 bits per core)
compares A, B, C every cycle
Voter output per bit: Y = A·B + B·C + A·C
Inputs to the cores (read data, grant, valid, error,
interrupts, reset) are not voted. They are distributed
monitor → detect → classify → isolate → save state →
reset all cores → restore state → verify (N cycles)
on failure: retry (M times) → system reset → safe state
Outputs: resynchronisation interrupt, core reset, target reset,
system-reset request, safe-state signal, FAULT pin
↓ request, address, write enable, byte enables, write data
PHX_BUS v1.0: D-CHANNEL (32-bit address, 32-bit data, request / grant / response-valid handshake)
Transient upset in one core's state
timeout, error response, reset or isolate
Bit flip in a data-memory word
system reset, then safe state + FAULT
IMEM contents, voter, bus, PHX_RM itself

Recovery sequence: a mismatch is detected and located; the two healthy cores save the processor state to DMEM through the voters; all three cores are reset together; the state is restored and the program resumes; PHX_RM then checks N cycles for agreement.
The CPU cluster presents one instruction port and one data port to the rest of the SoC, so the bus, memories and peripherals are identical for the one-core and three-core builds.
Implementation: one shared RTL for two tracks, an FPGA prototype and RTL-to-GDSII in the SAED 32 nm educational library. Fabrication is not planned in this phase.
Not part of this architecture: embedded FPGA fabric, dynamic partial reconfiguration, ECC on IMEM, debug module, boot loader, DMA, SPI, I²C.
